title: What is known about 1RB---_1RC1RF_1LD1RE_1LB1LD_0RB0RC_1RA0LF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_1RC1RF_1LD1RE_1LB1LD_0RB0RC_1RA0LF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

Seen at the moments the head, in state E, reaches a new cell on the right, the tape is a row of digits: 1^a 0 1^(4m1+1) 0 1^(4m2+1) 0 … 1^(4mk+1) 0 1^b E>0, blocks of 1s one more than a multiple of four, each followed by a single 0 (and a last run of b ones, b = 1 since step 877,024,800). In the 1011-step run 73 of the 82 such moments have exactly this form. Most digits are 0 or 1. The last digit grows by one at each new right cell (its block by four ones), and the time to the next new right cell doubles; meanwhile a 1 or a 2 walks left through the 0s, one digit per record. When it reaches the left part of the tape, the head visits the left end, the digits are rewritten and a new phase starts, with a new last digit.

At each new cell on the right in state E the tape reads 1^2 0, then digits 1^(4m+1) 0 (most of them 0 or 1), then a last digit that grows by one at each record, then 0 1 E>0. Between two records the head runs over the list many times; the time between records doubles. The visible change from one record to the next is a disturbance that moves one digit to the left: in the current phase a single digit 1 walking left through 0s.
verdict: The question is open. The machine can halt only from B> 1 0 1 (both directions in Lean). Its run is a clock at the right end of the tape: a block of 1s grows by four cells per tick and tick k sends the word beside it through 2k trips of the head — proved in Lean for every k and every word, whenever the 2k trips all return. Between clock phases a second clock, on the next block in, takes over; it is not yet proved. An exact accelerated run follows the machine to step 2.39·10248 without a halt.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 320 cells have been visited and 176 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.0). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.03).

claims.title: The halting context
claims.text: From B> 1 0 1 the machine reaches its halting transition (proved step by step, then step_none_iff). The halting transition is A reading a 1. A is entered only from F reading a 0 (F writes 1 and moves right), so the machine halts exactly when F has 0 1 under and after it. F is entered from B reading a 1 (moving right) or from F reading a 1 (moving left, and erasing it), so the only way in is B> 1 0 1. The converse is proved too: a configuration halts after exactly two more steps if and only if it is B> 1 0 1 (halt_iff_2), so a halting run from blank passes through it (halts_blank_pred_2).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: 11 shift rules over the words of the tape (for example (1)^n F> 1 becomes F> 1 (0)^n in n steps (F erases a run of 1s), E> (0111)^n becomes (1111)^n E> in 4n steps), proved for every n.

claims.title: No halt in the first 100,000,000,000 steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun.c runs 100,000,000,000 steps without a halt; the visited tape is 360 cells wide and holds 198 ones.

claims.title: Near misses
claims.text: F has never had 0 1 under it, and B has never had 1 0 1 ahead, in the first 1010 steps. B had 0 1 0 ahead 104 times (the last at step 877,024,667, at a visit to the left end); all its other contexts are periodic and harmless.

claims.title: The macro configuration
claims.text: At 73 of the 82 new right cells reached in state E in 1011 steps the tape is exactly 1^a 0 (1^(4m+1) 0)* 1^b E>0.

claims.title: Binary clock
claims.text: The gaps between consecutive new right cells double (for example 71,443,498, 142,886,824 and 285,773,694 steps just after step 10<sup>9</sup>), so the width grows like the logarithm of the step count.

claims.title: Phases and doubling
claims.text: In 3·10<sup>10</sup> steps the records on the right in state E fall into three phases, ending at steps 73,627 and 877,024,800 (each end follows a visit to the left end). Inside a phase the steps between records satisfy d<sub>k+1</sub> = 2d<sub>k</sub> + c with |c| ≤ 324; in phase 3 they are 56, 124, 260, 532, ..., 2,286,189,780, 4,572,379,564, 9,144,759,132 (c = 12 for the next seven, then between −324 and 180, then 4).

claims.title: The walking digit
claims.text: Read as digits m (blocks 1^(4m+1) 0, py/digits.py), the 28 records of phase 3 show the last digit going 1, 2, ..., 28 and a disturbance moving one digit left per record; from step 2,020,119,422 on it is a single 1 walking through 0s (the list 000000000001111000001000000000011110010011100210101010118[28] at step 19,166,542,786, one character per digit).

claims.title: No small finite-automata certificate
claims.text: A finite-automata-reduction search (a DFA of n states on one side of the head, the least co-closed NFA on (state × DFA state) + bottom for the other) finds no certificate with n ≤ 6, with the DFA on the left or on the right.

claims.title: The sweep and the merge (mirror image)
claims.text: On the mirror image of the machine (left and right swapped): rule_sweep: 0^4 E> 1^(6+4n) 0 becomes 0 0 0 1 0^(6+4n) F> 0 in 4n+10 steps; rule_merge: 0 0 0 1 E> 1 becomes E> 1^5 in 14 steps, for every n and all tapes around.

claims.title: The clock, for every k (mirror image)
claims.text: tick: for every j, every word W and all tapes L, if W reaches W' by 2j P-steps (each one a trip L 0^6 F> 0 W → L E> 1^6 0 W', for every L) of total cost E, then L 0^4 E> 1^(6+4j) 0 W reaches L E> 1^(6+4j+4) 0 W' in exactly E + 28·2j − 4 steps. Strong induction on j: sweep, one P-step, ticks 0, …, j−1, merge.

claims.title: The clock of this machine (right end)
claims.text: A mirror lemma (step_mir, steps_mir: one step of the mirror image is one step of the machine on the mirrored configuration) carries the tick over: tick_right_end and tick state the same clock for the machine itself, at the right end of the tape.

claims.title: The exact accelerated run
claims.text: holdouts/1RB0RA_0LC0RE_1LE1LD_0LE---_1LF0LC_1RA1LE/py/clock.py simulates cell by cell but does a tick at once when its 2k P-steps all come back (the theorem above; P computed by running the machine, P2k memoized). It gives the same time, block and word as tools/c/tmrun.c at all 81 visits of the right end in the first 2·1010 steps, and follows the run to step 2.39·10248 without a halt. Clock phases (first and last visit): 5.7718·108 (1^1) to 3.7457·1013 (1^161); 2.0070·1022 (1^1) to 6.5767·1026 (1^337); 6.7309·1026 (1^5) to 1.6673·1057 (1^741); 8.0977·10140 (1^1) to 7.7989·10245 (1^3245).

claims.title: The second regime
claims.text: Between the clock phases the end of the tape is 1^N 0 1 0 C>0: the block N one further in grows by 4 per visit while the time between visits doubles (from 3.8·1013 to 2.0·1022, from 1.67·1057 to 8.1·10140, and from 7.98·10245 to the end of the run, 814 visits). This is a clock one block further in; its tick is not covered by the theorem, so the accelerated run does these visits one at a time.

claims.title: The clock test (before the proof)
claims.text: From the visit at step 877,164,131 the word at each visit is the word at the previous one after 1024, 2048 and 4096 applications of one base map (the machine run).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: A normal tick cannot halt (the clock theorem). Halting needs B> 1 0 1, which would have to be built at the end of a phase or inside the second regime. Open: a proof of the second-regime tick, a closed form for P, and what a phase end does to the word.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RA_1LC1LE_1RA1LD_0LB0LC_1LF0RE_1LB--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1RE_1LC1RD_1LA1LC_0RA0RB_1RF0LE_1RA--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LA_1RC---_1RD1RA_1LE1RF_1LC1LE_0RC0RD up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows whether it halts. Started on a blank tape, this machine runs a clock at the right end of its tape: a block of 1s grows by four cells per tick and tick k applies one map P to the word beside it 2<sup>k</sup> times. The clock is proved in Lean for every tick whose 2<sup>k</sup> trips all return; an exact accelerated run follows it to 2.39·10<sup>248</sup> steps.

facts.text: Whenever its 2<sup>k</sup> trips all return, tick k applies P exactly 2<sup>k</sup> times, for every k and every word (Lean, via the mirror image).
Steps followed by the exact accelerated run, no halt.
Every halt passes through it, and it always halts (Lean: halt_ctx, halt_iff_2); never seen.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.0). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.03).
After 109 steps the tape spans 320 cells (25 left of the start, 203 right), with a density of 1s of 0.55.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: The one way to stop
html: The halting transition is A reading a 1. A is entered only from F reading a 0 (F writes 1 and moves right), so the machine halts exactly when F has 0 1 under and after it. F is entered from B reading a 1 (moving right) or from F reading a 1 (moving left, and erasing it), so the only way in is B> 1 0 1. So the machine halts exactly when it produces B> 1 0 1; Lean proves both directions (halt_ctx: the steps from there to the halt; halt_iff_2: nothing else halts two steps later).

sections.heading: A row of digits
html: Read each block 1^(4m+1) 0 as the digit m (written [m] when it is more than 9). The last moments in the 1011-step run when the head reached a new cell on the right in state E:
From row to row the last digit grows by one, the time doubles, and a small digit walks one place to the left through the 0s.

sections.heading: What a proof would need
html: A proof of the second clock's tick would let the accelerated run jump through it too. What decides halting is what a phase end does to the word: the halting context B> 1 0 1 would have to be built there.

sections.heading: A block that grows by four, a word that is run 2<sup>k</sup> times
html: Watch the tape at the moments the head, in state C, stands on a 0 just right of 1^L 0 at the right end. Along a phase L grows by four per visit and each visit takes twice as long as the previous one. Seen in the mirror (left and right swapped), the step from one visit to the next is a tick: the head sweeps the block into 0s, makes 2k trips through the word (each one application of a map P), and merges the block back four cells longer. That tick is proved in Lean for every k and every word, then carried to the machine itself by a mirror lemma.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1RE_1LC1RD_1LA1LC_0RA0RB_1RF0LE_1RA---: rename A→F, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→D, F→E; it is this table started in state B

summary: A clock at the right end: at each visit the block 1^(1+4k) has grown by 4 and the word beside it has gone through 2^k applications of one map P (one trip of the head) — proved in Lean for every k whenever the 2^k trips all return, on the mirror image of the machine. Between clock phases a second clock runs one block further in. Exact accelerated run to 2.39·10<sup>248</sup> steps, no halt; halting needs B> 1 0 1.
family: clock and word map (block grows by 4, right end)
